goals: Make shell verifier timeouts kill the whole POSIX process group on Linux and harden process-tree stress fixtures against spawn races. In src/verification/verifier.ts, spawn non-Windows verifyCommands with a dedicated process group and on timeout signal -pid with SIGTERM then a short SIGKILL escalation; Windows keeps direct pid kill. Preserve exit 124 TIMEOUT semantics and legacy 30s default when verifyTimeoutMs is absent. In tests/worker-process-tree.test.ts, before residual-bound and 512-member nested-group assertions, wait until the expected helper/group membership is observable via the ProcessInspector (fail on timeout rather than under-count). Keep exact-identity cleanup and fail-closed behavior unchanged. Add docs/evidence/LINUX_POSIX_VERIFIER_HARDENING.md recording host kernel/Node, focused commands, and pass counts for verifier-shell timeout override plus the two process-tree stress tests. Extend tests/verifier-shell.test.ts if needed to keep the contract-timeout wall-clock assertion meaningful.
nonGoals: Do not add systemd-run, launchd or daemon packaging.
Do not change DEFAULT_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_MS for legacy contracts.
Do not lower process-tree durable bounds or weaken fail-closed cleanup.
Do not claim pilot readiness or OS sandboxing.
verifyCommands: npx tsx --test --test-timeout=180000 --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern='contract timeout overrides|option timeout is the fallback|bounds residual evidence|cleans more than 16 external groups with a 512-member' tests/verifier-shell.test.ts tests/worker-process-tree.test.ts
deliverables: POSIX process-group kill for shell verifier timeouts.
Race-free process-tree stress waits on Linux.
Linux evidence document with exact commands and results.
forbidden: Do not leave shell grandchildren running after a verifier timeout on Linux.
Do not use process-name or broad kill for cleanup.
Do not skip the stress tests silently without a failing wait timeout.
